subject: Logic
title: Composition and Division
description: Learn Composition and Division in one minute.

hook.text: Every player on the team is great. Does that guarantee a great team? Not necessarily.

buildup.text: The fallacy of composition assumes what's true of the parts must be true of the whole.

discovery.text: Division does the reverse: the company is profitable, so every department must be profitable.

twist.text: Atoms are invisible, but objects made of atoms aren't. Properties don't always transfer.

climax.text: Wholes and parts can have entirely different properties. Check each level separately.

punchline.text: Parts don't always mirror the whole.

quiz.question: What does the fallacy of composition assume?
options: The whole is less than its parts
What's true of parts is true of the whole
